tool_schemas.name: discover
tool_schemas.description: Lists predicates available in a Prolog engine or session, optionally scoped to a specific loaded/compiled program, and returns a paged catalog of predicate entries filtered by origin/status/name prefix and ordered by the requested sort; pagination uses `limit` and an opaque `cursor` returned with each page. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if neither `session_id` nor `engine_id` is provided, if IDs do not match the required patterns, or if `limit`, `sort`, or filter enums are invalid. Raises UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN when you lack access to the referenced engine/session/program, and NOT_FOUND when the referenced `session_id`, `engine_id`, or `program_id` does not exist or is not visible to you.

engine_id.description: Prolog engine id to discover predicates from (if no session_id is provided).

session_id.description: Prolog session id to discover predicates from (preferred for session-specific/user-program predicates).

program_id.description: Prolog program id to scope discovery to a specific loaded/compiled program.

status.description: Filter predicate catalog entries by status.

name_prefix.description: Filter predicates whose name starts with this prefix.

limit.description: Maximum number of predicates to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for fetching the next page of results.

tool_schemas.name: exec
tool_schemas.description: Compiles/loads the provided Prolog `program` into a session and returns a program/session execution record (including the resulting program identifier and any compilation diagnostics). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR when `program` is missing or not a string, and CONFLICT when the target session cannot accept a new program because it is not in a loadable state (for example, already running or closed). Raises UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN if you are not allowed to execute programs on the engine/session and NOT_FOUND if the referenced execution context does not exist.

tool_schemas.name: query
tool_schemas.description: Runs the provided Prolog `query` against the currently loaded program in the active session and returns a persisted query-run record containing the produced solutions (or failure) and execution metadata. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR when `query` is missing or not a string, CONFLICT when a query is submitted without a loaded/compiled program or when the session is not in a queryable state, and NOT_FOUND when the referenced session/program context is missing. Raises UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN if you do not have permission to query the engine/session, and may raise QUOTA_EXCEEDED when your account or session has reached configured query limits.

tool_schemas.name: engines
tool_schemas.description: Lists Prolog engines visible to the caller, optionally filtered by status and engine_type, and returns a paged collection ordered by the requested sort; pagination uses `limit` and an opaque `cursor` returned with each page. Refuses with UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not authenticated, and FORBIDDEN if the caller lacks permission to list engines.

name_prefix.description: Filter engines whose name starts with this prefix.

limit.description: Maximum number of engines to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for fetching the next page of results.

tool_schemas.name: get_engine
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single Prolog engine by id and returns the engine record. Raises NOT_FOUND if the engine does not exist or is not visible to the caller, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not entitled to access it.

tool_schemas.name: create_session
tool_schemas.description: Creates a new Prolog session for the specified engine and returns the session record (including computed `expires_at`). Refuses with NOT_FOUND if the engine does not exist, CONFLICT if the engine is `disabled`, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not entitled to create sessions on the engine.

engine_id.description: Engine to create the session for.

ttl_seconds.description: Requested session TTL in seconds; capped by the engine's default/session policy.

tool_schemas.name: get_session
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single Prolog session by id and returns the session record. Raises NOT_FOUND if the session does not exist, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not entitled to access it.

tool_schemas.name: renew_session
tool_schemas.description: Renews/extends a Prolog session's expiration (sliding TTL) and returns the updated session record. Refuses with CONFLICT if the session is `expired` (must create a new session), and VALIDATION_ERROR if the requested extension exceeds the engine's maximum allowed (including the cap of `created_at + default_session_ttl_seconds` unless explicitly configured).

ttl_seconds.description: Requested additional TTL in seconds; applied subject to engine/session caps.

metadata.name: Prolog Execution and Querying
metadata.description: This backend stores Prolog execution sessions, uploaded/compiled programs, and query runs against a Prolog engine. Main workflows are: (1) inspect available predicates (discover) from a given engine/session, (2) submit a Prolog program to compile/load into a session (exec), and (3) run queries again
